# nirvana_storage_key (Resource)

An Object Storage Key: an S3 access key for a project's Buckets in one region.

The `secret` is returned only when the key is created. The provider keeps it in state from the create response and never re-reads it from the API, so treat the state as sensitive. Importing an existing key cannot recover its secret: `secret` stays null for an imported key. To get a new secret, replace the key (for example with `terraform apply -replace`).

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "nirvana_storage_key" "example_storage_key" {
  name = "ci-uploads"
  project_id = "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000"
  region = "us-sva-2"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the Object Storage Key.
- `project_id` (String) Project ID the Object Storage Key belongs to. The key can access the
project's Buckets in its region.
- `region` (String) Region the resource is in.
Available values: "us-sva-2", "us-wdc-1".

### Read-Only

- `access_key` (String) S3 access key ID.
- `created_at` (String) When the Object Storage Key was created.
- `id` (String) Unique identifier for the Object Storage Key.
- `secret` (String, Sensitive) S3 secret access key. It is only returned here and cannot be retrieved
again: store it securely, or delete the key and create a new one if it is
lost.
- `status` (String) Status of the resource.
Available values: "pending", "creating", "updating", "ready", "deleting", "deleted", "error", "suspended".
- `updated_at` (String) When the Object Storage Key was updated.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
$ terraform import nirvana_storage_key.example '<key_id>'
```
